history.summary: The platform verify callback may run more than once; the implementation rejected the second callback and could race.
history.resolution: Each valid callback is evaluated once in order with sticky rejection; regression tests added.

history.summary: Peer certificate chain count and bytes were unbounded.
history.resolution: 10-certificate and 262,144-byte bounds in transport and live collector; tests added. Security regression RED exited 1 before the fix; 118 passed after.

history.summary: Transport and trust decision were module-internal and unusable by future package targets.
history.resolution: Package-only surface; backend seam remains internal; 118 passed.

history.summary: Comments and docs claimed leaf-first certificate order, which neither the SDK header nor Apple documentation guarantees.
history.resolution: Naming and docs changed to platform callback order with explicitly no index semantics.

findings.summary: No real network or peer handshake is exercised.
The evaluator is synchronous and a slow evaluator may stall the handshake.
No transport-owned connect, read or write timeout.
A clean peer EOF is reported as a disconnected failure.
Outbound Data has no transport size cap.
The platform callback gives no documented meaning to certificate indices.
Source and tests are large (826 + 1174 lines before any later evidence-only edit), costing maintainability.
